entity.name: Trevor Gutierrez
entity.description: Independent software developer in Finland and the only person who has contributed to silosuite-crypto, a small end-to-end-encryption library (Rust, compiled to WebAssembly) published under Apache-2.0. I build privacy-respecting consumer tools where the privacy claim is enforced by architecture rather than policy: drafts and audience contact data are encrypted in the user's browser, under keys the server never holds. The funding solicited here goes to the one thing a small cryptography library most needs and can least afford: an independent external security review of the cryptographic core and its WebAssembly/JavaScript boundary, plus the open-source engineering to remediate findings and keep the library a clean, reusable public building block.

projects.name: silosuite-crypto
projects.description: A small, standalone end-to-end-encryption library in Rust, compiled to WebAssembly so any web application can encrypt user content client-side without trusting the server. In roughly 2,300 lines it composes established, widely-reviewed open primitives - XChaCha20-Poly1305-IETF authenticated encryption, Argon2id password-based key derivation, HKDF-SHA256, X25519 key agreement and sealed boxes, Ed25519 signatures, and BIP-39 recovery phrases - drawn from the RustCrypto, dalek-cryptography and rust-bitcoin projects. It implements no primitives of its own; its contribution is correct composition, an API designed to be hard to misuse, versioned ciphertext envelopes, memory zeroization, and a single Rust implementation shared by server and browser. Published under Apache-2.0 with continuous integration. The library is code-complete and pre-launch; an independent cryptographic audit and a WASM/JS-boundary application-security review are the funded goals, with the reports to be published in full.

channels.description: Direct SEPA bank transfer (Finland). Please e-mail for account details.

plans.name: Independent cryptographic audit
plans.description: Fixed-scope external audit of the cryptographic core by a specialist firm: construction and composition of the primitives, key management and lifecycle, and API misuse-resistance. The full report will be published. Amount is a market-sized estimate for a library of this size and scope.

plans.name: WASM/JS-boundary application-security review
plans.description: Separable external review of the WebAssembly/JavaScript boundary: preservation of constant-time behaviour and memory hygiene across Rust to WASM to JS, and absence of boundary-level leaks or misuse hazards. Report published in full.

plans.name: Remediation, documentation and release engineering
plans.description: Triage and remediation of audit findings with auditor re-test, published test vectors, documentation and integration examples, and packaging for crates.io and npm, billed at a cost-recovery rate.

plans.name: Goodwill plan
plans.description: Any amount toward the audit and open-source engineering above.
